key_insight: Scalable POD and DMD reveal dominant 3D flow structures and their temporal dynamics around a Formula 1 front wing while compressing approximately 6 TB of snapshots to 200 GB of modal data.
engineering_relevance: Identifying unsteady vortex dynamics can support aerodynamic diagnosis and reduced-order modeling of complex motorsport components.
method: Simulate the Imperial Front Wing at Re = 2.2 × 10^5 using spectral/hp-element LES in Nektar++.
Apply scalable POD and DMD through the open-source pyLOM framework.
Link DMD modes to flow mechanisms using point-probe spectra.
evidence_signal: The 49.72-million-degree-of-freedom simulation shows mean lift and drag coefficient differences of 2.24% and 2.87% versus reference data; probe spectra associate chord-based Strouhal numbers 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 with distinct flow mechanisms.
watch_item: Results concern one wing benchmark and Reynolds number; transferability to other geometries and operating conditions remains to be established.
paper_title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
